A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VISBIAS research. Their main text, algorithms, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite reorganization and graphical redesign.

before.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations across four scenarios, including demographic divergence scores, image-description analyses, and human judgments of 370 attribute correlations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds fictional-species evaluations, no-image controls, text-only form completion, and explicit–implicit distribution comparisons.

M1.justification: The four-scenario VISBIAS framework, CipherChat procedure, cyclic form shifts, GPT-4o response categorization, and KL-based correlation-ranking algorithm remain unchanged. Text-only evaluation applies the existing form-completion analysis under another input condition.

E1.justification: v3 extends evaluation to five fictional species—Orc, Murloc, Goblin, Dwarf, and Elf—and to text-only personal-information forms. It also tests explicit questions without images. These expand represented populations and input conditions beyond the retained human-image and visual-form scenarios.

E2.justification: The original model comparisons remain intact. The new text-only comparison adds Qwen-2.5-72B-Instruct alongside LLaMA-3.2-90B-Vision-Instruct, Gemini-1.5-Pro, and GPT-4o (Table 9). BiasDora receives additional discussion but is not newly evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include questions without images with and without CipherChat, text-form testing with matched prompt content, and gender/race-conditioned JSD comparisons between explicit and implicit outputs. Existing experiments retain their sample counts and temperatures. Newly described image filtering and form construction do not establish changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds fictional-species negative controls, a no-image ablation, a text-versus-visual-input investigation, and an analysis of explicit–implicit distribution similarity (Sections 4.1–4.3 and Appendix A.2). These address additional questions about demographic specificity, visual dependence, modality, and cross-task relationships.

E5.justification: Appendix C.1 newly reports standard deviations for questionnaire completion time (278.68 seconds) and annotator age (8.00 years). These describe participant/task variability, not uncertainty in model bias estimates. The existing three-annotator design and model sampling counts are unchanged; no new model-result confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Original quantitative tables and correlation-plot data are retained. New outcomes include fictional-species scores, default responses without images, twelve text-only attribute-pair results, and cross-task JSDs. For example, Table 9 reports GPT-4o's text-only Student-to-Age KLD as 20.99, marked not biased, and Section 4.3 reports a gender-conditioned education JSD of 0.063 for GPT-4V. These are additional results under new comparisons.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 and its marginal/conditional distributions and KL-ranking mathematics are unchanged. The additional analyses use empirical divergence measures without introducing new formal definitions, assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the four-scenario framework and principal bias findings. However, v3 removes the broad priority claim that VISBIAS is the first to jointly assess direct-judgment and assistance contexts, narrowing its asserted novelty (v2 Section 4; v3 Section 5).

C2.justification: v3 introduces interpretations involving RLHF regularization of human categories, fictional species as calibration for perceived bias, and shared representations underlying explicit and implicit associations. It also contrasts findings with BiasDora and adds a specific limitation acknowledging that backgrounds, lighting, and attire may drive observed associations.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents image-selection exclusions, automated Microsoft Word-to-PNG form construction using Python, and the composition and task statistics of 50 annotators. It also specifies model variants for text-only testing and shows additional collected-image examples. The existing code/data access statement, CipherChat prompt, attribute choices, and temperatures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds FairGamer and Qwen2.5 references, replaces several model-source citations, expands its comparison with BiasDora's reported findings, and removes the sweeping joint-assessment priority claim. Much of the remaining bibliography change consists of publication or title updates to retained works.

P1.justification: Most existing abstract, introduction, method, experiment, and conclusion prose is retained. v3 adds a Further Analysis section and an LLM-usage disclosure, makes local explanatory edits, and groups the former Appendices A–F into results, detailed settings, and human-study sections. This reorganizes supporting material without broadly rewriting the existing narrative.

P2.justification: All twenty correlation panels are redrawn with new categorical colors, triangle markers, and larger legend symbols while preserving their underlying results. v3 adds three result tables and an image montage, redistributes appendix tables and plots, and splits the existing questionnaire screenshots into separately captioned figures.

improvement.justification: The added no-image and text-only checks, annotator documentation, form-construction details, and background-confounding limitation provide a modest net improvement in empirical scrutiny and transparency while preserving the original evidence. The gain is limited: Section 4.1 does not directly test its RLHF explanation, and Section 4.3 does not explain how differing MCQ and form answer categories were aligned for JSD comparison.
